widgets.stem: If $X=\{2,-1\}$ and $Y=\{4,0\}$, find $X\times Y$. Tap all the ordered pairs that belong to $X\times Y$.
widgets.instrument: Spec example {"X":[1,2],"Y":[3,4,5]} — the student taps ordered pairs to build X×Y (decoys are added automatically). Small sets only: 2–3 numbers each, at most 4. Validator limits (parseMathWidget): X and Y are non-empty lists of numbers.

reading_fields.X: the set X as a list
reading_fields.Y: the set Y as a list

diagnostics.predicate_meaning: Built Y×X — the pairs are the right numbers in the wrong order
diagnostics.misconception_label: Treats X×Y and Y×X as the same
diagnostics.misconception_description: The student writes the pairs with the elements in the wrong order, or assumes X×Y gives the same set as Y×X.

hints.predicate_meaning: An incomplete product: some pairs of X×Y were not selected
hints.text: Take each element of X in turn and pair it with every element of Y. Check that no element of X is left with fewer pairs than the size of Y.

widgets.stem: If $X=\{2,-1\}$, find $X^2=X\times X$. Tap all the ordered pairs that belong to $X^2$.
widgets.instrument: Spec example {"X":[1,2],"Y":[3,4,5]} — the student taps ordered pairs to build X×Y (decoys are added automatically). Small sets only: 2–3 numbers each, at most 4. Validator limits (parseMathWidget): X and Y are non-empty lists of numbers.

reading_fields.X: the set X as a list
reading_fields.Y: the set Y as a list

hints.predicate_meaning: An incomplete product: some pairs of X×Y were not selected
hints.text: $X^2$ is X crossed with itself. Take each element of X as the first projection and pair it with every element of X.

widgets.stem: Represent graphically the function $f(x) = x + 2$. Drag the two points so the line is the graph.
widgets.instrument: Spec example {"mode":"equation","m":2,"b":-1} — the student DRAGS two lattice points and the line through them is drawn, with its equation updating live. In "equation" mode any two points on the correct line are accepted, so use it to ask for a line by its rule; m must be a whole number or the reciprocal of one, and b a whole number in −5..5. The other mode is {"mode":"points","through":[[-2,1],[3,4]]} — there the two named points ARE the answer. Validator limits (parseMathWidget): |m| is at most 5; in "points" mode the two points are distinct lattice points within ±5. Pipeline rule (stricter than the app; consistency review A10): in "points" mode neither named point, nor either point with its x and y exchanged, may sit at (-3, -2) or (1, 1) — the two handles open there, so the widget would start half-answered and a handle the student never moved could not be told from one she placed.

hints.predicate_meaning: Correct slope, wrong intercept — a line parallel to the answer
hints.text: Your line has the right lean but sits at the wrong height. Work out f(0) and see where the graph must meet the y-axis.

hints.predicate_meaning: Right gradient, wrong sign — the line leans the other way
hints.text: Check two more pairs in the table: as x increases, does f(x) go up or down?

hints.predicate_meaning: A vertical line, which has no slope and cannot be written y = mx + c
hints.text: Each x has exactly one image f(x), so the graph cannot be a vertical line. Use the table of pairs.

hints.predicate_meaning: Neither the slope nor the intercept matches
hints.text: Start by finding f(0), f(1) and f(-1) from the rule, then place the points from your table.
